questions.question: A cupboard does not contain:
questions.explanation: A cupboard is made of wood and is used to store clothes; a button is a small fastener on a garment, not something a cupboard is made of or meant to hold.

questions.question: My mother's brother is my ______.
questions.explanation: A mother's brother is one's maternal uncle (mama).

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom:
"Through thick and thin"

options.A: put the bees in a line

questions.explanation: 'Through thick and thin' means under all circumstances, in good times and bad.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
Effective communication is about more than just exchanging information. It's about understanding the emotion and intentions (1) ______ the information. As well as being able to clearly convey a message, you need to also (2) ______ in a way that gains the full meaning of what's being said and makes the other person feel heard and understood. For many of us, communicating more clearly and effectively requires learning some (3) ______ skills. Whether you're trying to improve communication with your spouse, kids, boss, or coworkers, learning these skills can (4) ______ your connections to others, build greater trust and respect, and (5) ______ teamwork, problem solving, and your overall social and emotional health.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. (1).
questions.explanation: We try to understand the emotion and intentions 'behind' the information, i.e. what lies underneath it.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. (2).
questions.explanation: The sentence is about gaining the full meaning of what is said and making the other person feel heard, so 'listen' fits.

questions.explanation: Learning skills that improve communication requires 'important' skills; 'wasteful' and 'trivial' contradict the positive tone.

questions.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी प्राचीन भारतीय आर्य भाषा है?
questions.explanation: The Old Indo-Aryan period (about 1500 BCE to 500 BCE) includes Vedic and Classical (Laukik) Sanskrit. Prakrit and Apabhramsha belong to the Middle Indo-Aryan period.

questions.question: इनमें से किस भाषा का विकास मागधी अपभ्रंश से हुआ है?
questions.explanation: Magahi, Maithili and Bhojpuri developed from Magadhi Apabhramsha. Bagheli belongs to Eastern Hindi (Ardhamagadhi) and Garhwali to the Pahari group.

questions.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा अन्तःस्थ व्यंजन है?
questions.explanation: There are four Antahstha vyanjan: य, र, ल, व. च is a sparsh (palatal) consonant and प is a sparsh (labial) consonant.

questions.question: 'प वर्ग' (प, फ, ब, भ, म) का उच्चारण स्थान क्या है?
questions.explanation: The प varg (प, फ, ब, भ, म) is pronounced with the lips, so its place of articulation is ओष्ठ (oshthya varna).

questions.question: 'प्रातः काल' शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग प्रयुक्त हुआ है?
questions.explanation: In 'प्रातः काल', the avyaya 'प्रातः' is used before 'काल' in the role of a prefix; 'अहकाल' and 'प्रात' are not valid splits of the word.

questions.question: सेना, दल, सभा और कक्षा जैसे शब्द किस प्रकार की संज्ञा हैं?
questions.explanation: सेना (army), दल (team), सभा (assembly) and कक्षा (class) each denote a group of persons or things, so they are samuhvachak sangya.

questions.question: 'आने वाला क्षण लाल नजर आता है।' वाक्य में रेखांकित शब्द 'क्षण' किस वचन में है?
questions.explanation: Here 'क्षण' refers to a single coming moment (आने वाला ... आता है), so it is ekvachan. The word can also be used in the plural, so 'always singular' is wrong.

questions.question: 'घड़ी' किस प्रकार की संज्ञा है?
questions.explanation: 'घड़ी' denotes a whole class of objects, not a particular one or a group, so it is a jativachak sangya.

questions.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द उत्तम पुरुषवाचक सर्वनाम नहीं है?
questions.explanation: 'तुम' is a madhyam purush (second person) pronoun. 'हमको' and 'मुझमें' are forms of the first person pronouns हम and मैं.

questions.question: किस वाक्य में विशेषण का प्रयोग नहीं हुआ है?
questions.explanation: In 'वह विद्यार्थी है', 'वह' is a pronoun and 'विद्यार्थी' is a noun complement, so there is no adjective. In 'वह लड़का', 'वह' is a pronominal adjective, and 'प्रबुद्ध' is a qualitative adjective.

questions.question: किस वाक्य में क्रिया के 'सातत्यबोधक पक्ष' का प्रयोग हुआ है?

options.A: वह स्नान करके मंदिर जाता है।
options.B: विद्यार्थी पुस्तकालय में बैठकर समाचार पत्र पढ़ते हैं।
options.C: मोहन अपनी कक्षा में पढ़ा रहा है।
options.D: राम ने खाना खा लिया है।

questions.explanation: 'पढ़ा रहा है' shows an action that is continuing, which is the सातत्यबोधक (continuous) aspect. The other two show habitual actions.

questions.question: किस विकल्प में शब्द-युग्म का अर्थ-भेद सही नहीं है?
questions.explanation: अनिल means air and अनल means fire; अंश means part and अंस means shoulder; कुल means lineage and कूल means bank. आवलंब/अवलंब means support and अविलंब means without delay, so 'अधर-विलोकित' is the wrong meaning.

questions.question: मधु + अरि की संधि कीजिए:
questions.explanation: उ + अ = व (yan swar sandhi), so मधु + अरि = मध्वरि. 'मद्वरि' has the wrong consonant and 'मध्वरी' has a long ई.

questions.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा अनेकार्थी शब्द 'अंक' का अर्थ नहीं है?
questions.explanation: The meanings of 'अंक' include lap, number, an act of a play and a mark; 'पृथ्वी' is not one of them.

questions.question: इनमें से कौन-सा 'घट' शब्द का अर्थ नहीं है?
questions.explanation: 'घट' means pitcher, body, heart/mind and also 'to decrease'; it does not mean group.

questions.question: "हीरक-सी समीर माला जप" पंक्ति में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.explanation: The comparative word 'सी' in 'हीरक-सी' compares one thing to another, which makes it Upma alankar.

questions.question: जब एक या अनेक वर्णों की आवृत्ति एक ही क्रम में केवल एक बार हो, तब कौन-सा अलंकार होता है?
questions.explanation: A single repetition of one or more letters in the same order is Chhekanupras. Repetition many times is Vrityanupras, and repetition of words with a change of meaning in context is Latanupras.

questions.question:
गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।
हम मनुष्य कुछ न कुछ बनने का सपना देखते हैं। अपने सपने को साकार करने के लिए हम उसे अपना आधार और अपना लक्ष्य बनाते हैं और उसी सपने के आधार पर अपने भविष्य की नींव रखने लगते हैं। हमारा लक्ष्य कुछ भी हो सकता है: हम डॉक्टर, इंजीनियर, राजनेता, अभिनेता, सरकारी कर्मचारी या शिक्षक बनने की सोच सकते हैं। हमारी शिक्षा का स्तर ही उस लक्ष्य तक पहुँचने का मार्ग है; शिक्षा ही हमें लक्ष्य तक ले जाती है और उसे साकार करती है। शिक्षा व्यक्ति के जीवन में एक अनमोल रत्न के समान है, जिसे न कोई चुरा सकता है और न मिटा सकता है। जब यक्ष ने पूछा, 'परदेश में मनुष्य का साथी कौन है?', तब युधिष्ठिर ने उत्तर दिया, 'विद्या'। महाभारत में युधिष्ठिर और यक्ष के इस संवाद से स्पष्ट है कि प्राचीन काल से ही मानव जीवन में शिक्षा का महत्त्व रहा है।

लेखक ने अपनी बात की प्रामाणिकता सिद्ध करने के लिए कौन-सा उदाहरण प्रस्तुत किया है?

options.D: युधिष्ठिर और यक्ष के संवाद का

questions.explanation: The author cites the Yaksha-Yudhishthira dialogue from the Mahabharata to prove that education has always been important.

गद्यांश के अनुसार परदेश में मनुष्य का साथी है:
questions.explanation: Yudhishthira answered that 'Vidya' (knowledge) is a person's companion in a foreign land.

गद्यांश का सबसे उपयुक्त शीर्षक है:
questions.explanation: The central idea of the passage is the importance of education in human life; labour is not discussed at all.

questions.explanation: The passage says education is like a precious gem that no one can steal or erase.

questions.question: 'युद्ध में स्थिर रहने वाला' वाक्यांश के लिए एक शब्द चुनिए:
questions.explanation: The one word for 'युद्ध में स्थिर रहने वाला' is 'युधिष्ठिर'. युद्ध बंदी/कैदी means prisoner of war and युद्धपोत means warship.

questions.question: During Gandhiji's Non-Cooperation Movement, people were urged to give up liquor, which caused a heavy loss of government revenue. To encourage people to drink again, the government of one province circulated a list of prominent persons who drank. Name the province.
questions.explanation: The fall in excise revenue due to the liquor boycott led the Bihar government to circulate a list of eminent persons who drank liquor.

questions.question: In pre-independence India, who among the following supported the Swaraj Party in the Central Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: M.A. Jinnah, leader of the Independents in the Central Legislative Assembly, cooperated with the Swaraj Party there.

questions.question: Why was there a mass movement in India against the arrival of the Simon Commission?

options.A: Indians never wanted a review of the working of the Act of 1919
options.B: The Simon Commission recommended the abolition of dyarchy in the provinces
options.C: The Simon Commission proposed abolishing the provincial legislatures
options.D: There was no Indian member in the Simon Commission

questions.explanation: All seven members of the Simon Commission (1927) were British, so Indians boycotted it with the slogan 'Simon Go Back'.

questions.question: The 1929 session of the Indian National Congress is significant in the history of the freedom movement because in this session:

options.A: attainment of Poorna Swaraj was adopted as the goal of the Congress
options.B: self-government was declared as the objective of the Congress
options.D: the Civil Disobedience Movement was withdrawn

questions.explanation: At the Lahore session (1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, Poorna Swaraj (complete independence) was adopted as the goal.

questions.question: With reference to Gandhi's Dandi March, which of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.A: It was a march from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi village.
options.B: Its specific purpose was to protest against the salt tax.
options.C: On reaching the seashore, Gandhi manufactured salt.

questions.explanation: On 6 April 1930, Gandhi broke the salt law symbolically by picking up a handful of natural salt from the shore; he did not manufacture salt.

questions.question: For the Karachi session of the Indian National Congress in 1931, presided over by Sardar Patel, who drafted the resolution on Fundamental Rights and the Economic Programme?
questions.explanation: The resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme at Karachi (1931) was drafted by Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.concept: Resignation of Shri Krishna Sinha ministry
questions.question: Why did the elected government of Bihar formed by Shri Krishna Singh resign in February 1938?

options.A: Due to Gandhiji's satyagraha movement against the British
options.B: To take part in India's freedom movement
options.C: Over the issue of releasing political prisoners
options.D: Due to differences with the Muslim League

questions.explanation: The Governor refused to allow the release of political prisoners, so Dr. Shri Krishna Sinha's ministry resigned in February 1938.

questions.question:
The 'Quit India Movement' was the result of:
1. the frustration of Indians with the Cripps proposals
2. the threat of a Japanese invasion of India
3. Gandhiji's writings inciting countrymen to adopt violent means
4. a resolution passed by the A.I.C.C. in August 1942
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.explanation: The failure of the Cripps Mission, the fear of a Japanese invasion and the AICC's Quit India resolution of 8 August 1942 led to the movement. Gandhi never incited violence, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.question: Which of the following share a common border with Nepal?

options.A: Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bhutan and Punjab
options.B: Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Sikkim and West Bengal
options.D: Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Bihar and Assam

questions.explanation: Five Indian states border Nepal: Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Sikkim.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the biodiversity hotspots found in India?
questions.explanation: The biodiversity hotspots in India are the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands).

questions.question: As we move from south to north, from the plains to the Himalaya, what do we find?
questions.explanation: The Himalaya are young fold mountains formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates.

questions.question: The Tungabhadra river is a tributary of which of the following rivers?
questions.explanation: The Tungabhadra is a major right-bank tributary of the Krishna river.

questions.question: In which district of Bihar is Kanwar (Kabar) Lake located?
questions.explanation: Kanwar Lake, Asia's largest freshwater oxbow lake and a Ramsar site, is in Begusarai district of Bihar.

questions.question: Which place(s) in India receive the maximum rainfall during the winter season?
questions.explanation: The retreating (north-east) monsoon gives the Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu its heaviest rain in winter. Western disturbances give only light winter rain in the north-west.

questions.question: Which tree is the most dominant species of the tropical moist deciduous forests of India?
questions.explanation: Teak is the dominant species of tropical moist deciduous forests (with sal, shisham, bamboo and arjun). Deodar and chir pine are Himalayan conifers, and sundari grows in mangrove forests.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements and state which is/are correct:
1. Natural gas is found in the Gondwana layers.
2. Mica is found in abundance in Koderma district.
3. Dharwar is famous for petroleum.
questions.explanation: Gondwana rocks are known for coal and Dharwar rocks for metallic minerals; petroleum and natural gas occur in tertiary sedimentary rocks. Koderma (Jharkhand) is the mica capital of India, so only statement 2 is correct.

questions.question: Which of the following devices converts electrical energy into mechanical energy?
questions.explanation: An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy. A dynamo does the reverse, and a transformer changes AC voltage levels.

questions.question: Which of the following gives three consecutive colours of the visible spectrum (VIBGYOR) in the correct order?
questions.explanation: The spectrum order is Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red, so Blue, Green, Yellow are consecutive. 'Violet, Blue, Red' skips colours and the other two are out of order.

questions.question: Why are convex mirrors used as rear-view mirrors in motorcycles?

options.B: It makes the image appear smaller than the actual object
options.C: It forms an inverted, magnified image
options.D: It forms an erect, diminished image with a wide field of view

questions.explanation: A convex mirror always forms an erect, virtual and diminished image, giving a much wider field of view of the traffic behind. Making the image small is only a side effect, not the reason.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is wrong?

options.D: The particles of solids are closely packed.

questions.explanation: Solids have both a definite shape and a definite volume, so the statement that solids have an indefinite shape is wrong.

questions.question: A molecule of benzene has ______ double bonds.
questions.explanation: Benzene (C6H6) has a ring with 3 alternating double bonds and 3 single bonds between carbon atoms.

questions.question: ______ is the study of the biology and behaviour of primates such as monkeys, apes and orangutans.
questions.explanation: Primatology is the study of primates. Anthropology studies humans and ethnobotany studies the relationship between people and plants.

questions.question: What is the alternative term for the uterus?
questions.explanation: The uterus is also called the womb (Greek: hystera). The ureter carries urine from the kidney to the bladder.

questions.question: Who invented the first pacemaker?
questions.explanation: Canadian engineer John Hopps built the first external cardiac pacemaker in 1950. Virginia Apgar devised the Apgar score and Christiaan Barnard performed the first human heart transplant.

questions.question: Tap A can fill a tank in 10 hours and tap B in 5 hours. Tap C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three taps are opened simultaneously, how much time will it take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/10 + 1/5 - 1/20 = (2 + 4 - 1)/20 = 5/20 = 1/4, so the tank fills in 4 hours.

questions.question: Driving at 48 km/hr, Barun reached his destination 2 minutes early. If he drove at 42 km/hr, he would reach 1 minute late. What distance does Barun have to drive?
questions.explanation: Time difference = 3 minutes = 1/20 hr. d/42 - d/48 = 6d/2016 = d/336 = 1/20, so d = 16.8 km.

questions.question: If x and y are two positive numbers such that x² + y² = 8 and xy = 4, find the value of (x + y).
questions.explanation: (x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy = 8 + 8 = 16, so x + y = 4 (taking the positive root).

questions.question: The traffic lights at three consecutive intersections change every 35 seconds, 42 seconds and 90 seconds respectively. If they change together at 8:00:00, after how much time will they change together again?
questions.explanation: LCM(35, 42, 90) = 2 x 3² x 5 x 7 = 630 seconds = 10 minutes 30 seconds.

questions.question: The ratio between two numbers is 5 : 9. If 6 is added to both numbers, the ratio becomes 2 : 3. The original numbers are:
questions.explanation: Let the numbers be 5x and 9x. (5x + 6)/(9x + 6) = 2/3 gives 15x + 18 = 18x + 12, so x = 2 and the numbers are 10 and 18.

questions.question: The mean of 36 numbers was found to be 42. Later it was discovered that a number 47 was mistakenly read as 41. Find the correct mean (rounded to two decimal places).
questions.explanation: The total increases by 47 - 41 = 6, so the correct mean = 42 + 6/36 = 42.1666... ≈ 42.17.

questions.question: The ratio of boys to girls in a school is 3 : 2. If 20% of the boys and 25% of the girls get scholarships, what percentage of students do NOT get scholarships?
questions.explanation: Take 300 boys and 200 girls. Without scholarship: 80% of 300 = 240 and 75% of 200 = 150, so 390/500 = 78%.

questions.concept: Equal SP, equal gain and loss
questions.question: A person sold 2 items for ₹4000 each, making a profit of 15% on one and a loss of 15% on the other. Find his overall profit or loss (rounded to the nearest rupee).
questions.explanation: CP1 = 4000/1.15 = 3478.26 and CP2 = 4000/0.85 = 4705.88, total CP = 8184.14 against SP 8000, so loss ≈ ₹184. (Equal SP with equal gain and loss % always gives a loss.)

questions.question: Which is the biggest annual festival of the Hattee tribe of the Trans-Giri region of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Hattee community of the Trans-Giri area of Sirmaur district celebrates the Maghi festival as the 'Boda' festival, its biggest annual festival.

questions.question: When was RBI's Financial Literacy Week 2025, with the theme 'Financial Literacy - Women's Prosperity', observed?
questions.explanation: RBI observed Financial Literacy Week 2025 from 24 to 28 February 2025 on the theme 'Financial Literacy - Women's Prosperity'. (The source key marked 24 to 28 January, which does not match RBI's announcement.)

questions.question: Which IIT has developed the indigenous space chip IRIS?
questions.explanation: IIT Madras developed IRIS, an indigenous SHAKTI-based microprocessor chip for space applications, together with ISRO.

questions.question: Who has been honoured with the 'Forbes India Leadership Awards'?
questions.explanation: Jay Shah, former BCCI secretary and ICC chairman, was honoured for his contribution to sports administration.

questions.question: Which state topped in installations under the 'PM Surya Ghar' scheme?
questions.explanation: Gujarat ranked first in the country in rooftop solar installations under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana.

questions.question: Which decommissioned ship of the Indian Navy is being converted into India's first underwater museum?
questions.explanation: The decommissioned landing ship INS Guldar is being turned into India's first underwater museum off Sindhudurg, Maharashtra.

questions.question: In the Union Budget 2025-26, the fiscal deficit is estimated at what percentage of GDP?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2025-26 estimates the fiscal deficit for FY 2025-26 at 4.4% of GDP (4.8% was the revised estimate for 2024-25).

questions.question: Where was the first phase of the 'Khelo India Winter Games 2025' inaugurated?
questions.explanation: The first phase of the Khelo India Winter Games 2025 (ice events) was inaugurated in Leh, Ladakh; the second phase (snow events) was held in Gulmarg.

questions.question: In CPU scheduling, which algorithm can suffer from the 'convoy effect', where a large process blocks smaller processes?
questions.explanation: In non-preemptive FCFS, short processes queue behind a long CPU-bound process, which is the convoy effect.

questions.question: In an operating system, when does 'thrashing' occur?

options.A: When no process is running in the system
options.B: When a process goes into a deadlock
options.C: When the system spends too much time in paging activity, reducing performance
options.D: When the CPU is idle waiting for I/O

questions.explanation: Thrashing happens when the OS spends more time swapping pages in and out than executing processes.

questions.question: An integer variable used for process synchronization that is accessed only through two operations, wait() and signal(), is called a:
questions.explanation: A semaphore is an integer variable accessed only through the atomic operations wait() (P) and signal() (V).

questions.question: In computer architecture, when does a 'data hazard' occur in pipelining?

options.A: When two or more instructions try to use the same hardware resource
options.B: When the pipeline is disrupted by a branch instruction
options.D: When an instruction needs the result of a previous instruction that is not yet available

questions.explanation: A data hazard (RAW, WAR, WAW) occurs when an instruction depends on the result of an earlier instruction still in the pipeline. Competing for the same hardware is a structural hazard and a branch disruption is a control hazard.

questions.question: The technique for implementing virtual memory in which physical memory is divided into fixed-size blocks is called:
questions.explanation: Paging divides physical memory into fixed-size frames and logical memory into pages of the same size. Segmentation uses variable-sized segments.

questions.question: In cache memory, what is the main disadvantage of the direct mapping technique?

options.C: It needs a complex replacement algorithm
options.D: High probability of conflict between memory blocks that map to the same cache index

questions.explanation: In a direct-mapped cache each block maps to exactly one line, so blocks sharing an index keep evicting each other (conflict misses). Direct mapping is actually fast and simple.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of De Morgan's theorems?
questions.explanation: De Morgan's laws are (A · B)′ = A′ + B′ and (A + B)′ = A′ · B′. A + A′ = 1 is the complement law, and A · A′ is 0, not 1.

questions.question: In the ACID properties of a database transaction, what does 'Atomicity' mean?

options.A: The database always remains in a consistent state.
options.B: Concurrent transactions remain isolated from each other.
options.D: A transaction is either executed completely or not at all.

questions.explanation: Atomicity means all-or-nothing execution. 'Always consistent' is Consistency, 'isolated' is Isolation and 'survive failures' is Durability.

questions.question: In SQL, which clause is used to combine data (columns) from two or more tables?
questions.explanation: JOIN combines columns from two or more tables based on a related column. UNION stacks result rows of compatible queries.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of creating an index in a database?

options.A: To increase the speed of data retrieval

questions.explanation: An index gives a fast lookup path (for example a B-tree) so rows can be found without scanning the whole table. It actually uses extra storage.

questions.question: Which process does TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) use to establish a connection?
questions.explanation: TCP establishes a connection with a three-way handshake: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK.

questions.question: What is the main function of the Domain Name System (DNS)?

options.C: Translating domain names into IP addresses

questions.explanation: DNS resolves human-readable domain names into IP addresses. E-mail uses SMTP and file transfer uses FTP.

questions.question: What is the MAC address of a Network Interface Card (NIC) called?
questions.explanation: The MAC address is the hardware (physical) address burned into the NIC. The IP address is the logical address.

questions.question: A network device that only regenerates and rebroadcasts signals but does not filter traffic is called a:
questions.explanation: A repeater works at the physical layer and only regenerates the signal; routers and bridges filter traffic using addresses.

questions.question: In asymmetric cryptography, what type of keys are used?

options.D: A pair of a public key and a private key

questions.explanation: Asymmetric (public-key) cryptography uses a linked key pair: the public key to encrypt and the private key to decrypt.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a firewall?

options.C: To speed up the internet connection
options.D: To filter network traffic based on predefined security rules

questions.explanation: A firewall monitors and filters incoming and outgoing traffic according to configured security rules.

questions.question: In a graph data structure, which traversal algorithm uses a queue?
questions.explanation: BFS visits vertices level by level using a FIFO queue; DFS uses a stack (or recursion).

questions.question: Which of the following is a self-balancing binary search tree?
questions.explanation: An AVL tree keeps the heights of child subtrees within 1 of each other. A B-tree is a balanced multi-way (not binary) tree and a heap is not a search tree.

questions.question: What problem does Dijkstra's algorithm solve?
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's greedy algorithm finds the shortest paths from one source to all vertices in a graph with non-negative weights. MST is solved by Prim's or Kruskal's algorithm.

questions.question: In the analysis of algorithms, which notation is used to represent the worst-case time complexity of an algorithm?
questions.explanation: Big O gives an asymptotic upper bound and is the standard way to express worst-case complexity. Omega is a lower bound and Theta a tight bound.

questions.question: In OOP, how is runtime polymorphism achieved?
questions.explanation: Runtime (dynamic) polymorphism in C++ uses virtual functions called through base-class pointers or references. Overloading and templates are compile-time.

questions.question: In C++, a class that has at least one pure virtual function is called a:
questions.explanation: A class with at least one pure virtual function (declared = 0) is an abstract class and cannot be instantiated.

questions.question: In C++, what is used to implement generic programming?
questions.explanation: Function and class templates parameterise code by type, which is generic programming in C++.

questions.question: The keywords used for exception handling in C++ are:
questions.explanation: C++ exception handling encloses code in 'try', signals errors with 'throw' and handles them in 'catch'.

questions.question: The characteristic of the Waterfall Model of software development is:

options.A: It is a linear-sequential approach where each phase must be completed before the next
options.D: Customer feedback is taken after every short sprint

questions.explanation: The Waterfall model is linear and sequential: requirements, design, coding, testing and deployment, each finished before the next begins.

questions.concept: Full form and use of CSS
questions.question: What is the full form of CSS and why is it used?

options.A: Computer Style Sheets; for styling computers
options.B: Cascading Style Sheets; for the presentation and styling of web pages
options.C: Creative Style Sheets; for designing graphics
options.D: Colorful Style Sheets; for colouring text

questions.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets and separates the presentation and styling of web pages from their HTML structure.

questions.question: A website whose content stays fixed for the user and does not use server-side scripting is called a:
questions.explanation: A static website serves fixed HTML/CSS/JS files without server-side processing. Responsive refers to layout adapting to screen size.

questions.question: Which image file format uses lossy compression, resulting in a slight loss of quality?
questions.explanation: JPEG uses lossy (DCT-based) compression. PNG and GIF use lossless compression.

questions.question: What is the base of the hexadecimal number system?
questions.explanation: Hexadecimal has base (radix) 16 and uses digits 0 to 9 and letters A to F.

questions.question: In a microprocessor, what does the number of address lines determine?

options.B: The width of the data bus
options.D: The maximum memory that can be addressed

questions.explanation: With N address lines a processor can address 2^N memory locations.

questions.question: What is the core or central component of an operating system called?
questions.explanation: The kernel is the core of the OS that manages the CPU, memory, interrupts and devices. The shell is the user interface to it.

questions.question: In what is processor speed generally measured?
questions.explanation: Processor clock speed is measured in gigahertz (billions of cycles per second). MB measures storage and DPI measures print/display resolution.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of RAID storage technology?

options.A: To increase the system's processing speed
options.C: To improve data redundancy and performance

questions.explanation: RAID (Redundant Array of Independent Disks) combines several disks for fault tolerance (redundancy) and better I/O performance.

questions.question: The 'ping' command in a network is used to:

options.B: Test connectivity and response time (latency) to a host

questions.explanation: Ping sends ICMP Echo Request messages and waits for Echo Replies to check reachability and round-trip time.

questions.question: In the context of web browsing, what is a 'cookie'?

options.B: A small text file stored on the user's computer by a website

questions.explanation: A cookie is a small piece of data a website stores in the browser to remember sessions and preferences; it is not a virus.

questions.question: If both inputs of an XOR gate are the same (0 and 0, or 1 and 1), what will be the output?
questions.explanation: XOR outputs 1 only when its inputs differ, so for identical inputs the output is 0.

questions.question: The process of converting source code into an executable file involves:
questions.explanation: The compiler translates source code into object files, and the linker combines them with libraries into an executable.

questions.question: What is the cycle of fetching, decoding and executing an instruction by a processor called?
questions.explanation: The fetch-decode-execute sequence for one instruction is the instruction cycle; it is made of one or more machine cycles, each of several clock cycles.

questions.question: The main advantage of 'Cloud Computing' is:

options.C: Access to on-demand computing resources via the internet

questions.explanation: Cloud computing delivers servers, storage, databases and software on demand over the internet, usually pay-as-you-go.

questions.question: In cryptography, what does a 'Digital Signature' ensure?
questions.explanation: A digital signature proves who sent the data (authenticity), that it was not altered (integrity), and that the sender cannot deny it (non-repudiation). Confidentiality comes from encryption.

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for routing and logical addressing?
questions.explanation: The Network layer (Layer 3) handles routing of packets and logical (IP) addressing.

questions.question: Which network device operates at the Data Link Layer of the OSI model?
questions.explanation: A switch forwards frames using MAC addresses at Layer 2. A hub works at Layer 1 and a router at Layer 3.

questions.question: In which topology are all nodes connected to a central device?
questions.explanation: In a star topology every node connects to a central hub or switch.

questions.question: Which of the following protocols is used for sending e-mail?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends e-mail; POP3/IMAP retrieve it.

questions.question: What is the size of an IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: An IPv6 address is 128 bits long, compared with 32 bits for IPv4.

questions.question: What is the range of 'Well-Known Ports'?
questions.explanation: IANA reserves ports 0 to 1023 as well-known ports (HTTP 80, HTTPS 443, SSH 22). 1024 to 49151 are registered and 49152 to 65535 dynamic/private ports.

questions.question: A type of malware that disguises itself as legitimate software is called a:
questions.explanation: A Trojan horse pretends to be useful software to trick users into installing it. A worm self-replicates and spyware secretly collects data.

questions.question: What is the process of converting plaintext into ciphertext called?
questions.explanation: Encryption turns readable plaintext into ciphertext using a key; decryption reverses it. Hashing is one-way and not meant to be reversed.

questions.question: A cyber attack in which a server is flooded with traffic to make it unavailable is called:
questions.explanation: A DoS (or DDoS) attack overwhelms a server with traffic so legitimate users cannot be served.

questions.question: At which layer of the OSI model does an application-level gateway (proxy) firewall operate?
questions.explanation: An application-level gateway (proxy firewall) inspects application data such as HTTP or FTP commands, so it works at the Application layer. Packet filters work at the Network/Transport layers.

questions.question: Which of the following uniquely identifies a tuple in a relation but may contain extra (redundant) attributes?
questions.explanation: A super key is any set of attributes that uniquely identifies a tuple, even if it has extra attributes. A candidate key is a minimal super key.

questions.question: A relation is in BCNF if, for every non-trivial functional dependency X → Y, X is a ______.
questions.explanation: BCNF requires the determinant X of every non-trivial FD X → Y to be a super key of the relation.

questions.question: In a relational database, a row is also called a(n) ______.
questions.explanation: In relational terms a table is a relation, a column is an attribute and a row is a tuple.

questions.question: The number of tuples (rows) in a relation is called its ______.
questions.explanation: Cardinality is the number of rows; degree is the number of columns (attributes).

questions.question: Which of the following is a Data Definition Language (DDL) command?
questions.explanation: CREATE, ALTER, DROP and TRUNCATE are DDL. SELECT and INSERT are DML (data query/manipulation).

questions.question: Which is a Data Manipulation Language (DML) command in SQL?
questions.explanation: UPDATE is a DML command. GRANT and REVOKE are DCL commands and CREATE is a DDL command.

questions.question: Which of the following is an aggregate function in SQL?
questions.explanation: AVG (like COUNT, SUM, MIN and MAX) is an aggregate function that works on a set of rows. NOW, UPPER and ROUND are scalar functions.

questions.question: Which type of join returns all rows from the left table and the matching rows from the right table?
questions.explanation: A LEFT (OUTER) JOIN keeps every row of the left table and fills unmatched right-side columns with NULL.

questions.question: A relation has a degree of 5 and a cardinality of 10. If 2 attributes and 3 tuples are removed, what will be the new degree and cardinality?
questions.explanation: Degree = 5 - 2 = 3 and cardinality = 10 - 3 = 7.

questions.question: Which DDL command removes all rows from a table at once, without a WHERE clause, while keeping the table structure?
questions.explanation: TRUNCATE TABLE is a DDL command that removes all rows and keeps the structure. DELETE is DML and works row by row, DROP TABLE removes the table itself, and ALTER changes its structure.

questions.question: Which part of the CPU performs arithmetic and logical operations?
questions.explanation: The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations; the control unit directs operations and registers hold data temporarily.

questions.question: Which bus carries memory addresses from the processor to other components?
questions.explanation: The unidirectional address bus carries memory addresses from the CPU to memory and I/O.

questions.question: Where is frequently accessed data from main memory stored for faster access?
questions.explanation: Fast SRAM cache sits between the CPU and main memory and holds frequently used data.

questions.question: What are the main stages of an instruction cycle?
questions.explanation: The instruction cycle consists of fetching the instruction, decoding it and executing it.

questions.question: Which type of memory is non-volatile and typically contains the bootstrap loader?
questions.explanation: ROM (or flash/EEPROM firmware) is non-volatile and holds the BIOS/UEFI bootstrap loader. RAM and cache are volatile.

questions.question: What is the result of the hexadecimal subtraction (ABC)₁₆ − (123)₁₆?
questions.explanation: Digit by digit with no borrow: C(12) - 3 = 9, B(11) - 2 = 9, A(10) - 1 = 9, giving (999)₁₆.

questions.question: What range of numbers can be represented using an 8-bit unsigned binary representation?
questions.explanation: 8 unsigned bits represent 0 to 2⁸ - 1 = 255. -128 to +127 is the 8-bit signed (2's complement) range.

questions.question: What is the octal equivalent of the binary number 11011101?
questions.explanation: Group the bits in threes from the right: 011 011 101 = 3 3 5, so the answer is (335)₈.

questions.question: What is the 1's complement of the binary number 10110010?
questions.explanation: 1's complement inverts every bit: 10110010 becomes 01001101. 01001110 is the 2's complement.

questions.question: How many 1s will be in the binary representation of the decimal expression 2¹⁰ + 2⁵ + 2¹ + 1?
questions.explanation: 2¹⁰ + 2⁵ + 2¹ + 2⁰ = 1059 = 10000100011₂, with one 1 for each distinct power: exactly 4 ones.

questions.question: The Boolean expression A′B + A′B′ is equivalent to ______.
The simplified form of the Boolean expression XY + X′Z + YZ is:
questions.explanation: By the consensus theorem, XY + X′Z + YZ = XY + X′Z; the term YZ is redundant.

questions.question: According to De Morgan's law, (A + B)′ is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: The complement of a sum equals the product of the complements: (A + B)′ = A′ · B′.

questions.question: The Boolean expression (A + B)(A + B′) is equal to:
If x is a Boolean variable, what is x ⊕ x (x XOR x) equal to?
questions.explanation: XOR of any variable with itself is 0, since 0 ⊕ 0 = 0 and 1 ⊕ 1 = 0.

questions.question: In a two-valued Boolean algebra, what is the maximum number of different Boolean functions of 3 variables?
questions.explanation: 3 variables give 2³ = 8 truth-table rows, and each row can be 0 or 1, so there are 2⁸ = 256 functions.

questions.question: The simplified form of the Boolean function F = A′B′C′ + A′BC′ + AB′C′ is:
questions.explanation: A′B′C′ + A′BC′ = A′C′, and A′C′ + AB′C′ = C′(A′ + AB′) = C′(A′ + B′).

questions.question: Which of the following logic gates is also called a universal gate?
questions.explanation: NAND and NOR are universal gates because any Boolean function can be built using only one of them.

questions.question: The output of a 2-input NOR gate is 1 only when:
questions.explanation: NOR = (A + B)′, which is 1 only when A = 0 and B = 0.

questions.question: The output of an Exclusive-OR (XOR) gate is 0 when the inputs are:
questions.explanation: XOR gives 0 when the inputs match (0 ⊕ 0 = 0, 1 ⊕ 1 = 0) and 1 when they differ. 'Both 1' and 'only when both are 0' are each only one half of the rule.
